scene: A bounded, deduplicated three-family orbital population, the HYG reference sky and retained Sydney ISS pass.

observerPreset.name: Sydney
observerPreset.use: WGS84 geodetic surface viewpoint; geometric horizon and an idealised dark stellar sky.

sky.model: J2000 catalogue directions with time-dependent precession, nutation and Earth rotation. Proper motion, annual aberration, parallax, refraction and observing conditions omitted.
sky.surfaceVisibility: Authored twilight fade: full at solar altitude <= -18 degrees, zero at >= -6 degrees. No local atmosphere, weather, terrain or satellite brightness model.

pass.name: ISS / ZARYA
pass.rule: Complete ISS pass >=20 degrees, Sun <=−6 degrees over Sydney in the declared window; whole-second peak sampling and millisecond geometric horizon crossings. Not an optical visibility prediction.

geography.name: Natural Earth 1:110m land
geography.delivery: Bundled into the hashed application asset; offline reproduction, no provider fetch in CI or browsers.
geography.limits: Generalised global geography, not local coast accuracy, terrain, a Sydney skyline or observing conditions.

playback.autoplay: One-minute camera journey in visible, non-reduced-motion sessions after source readiness; once per page load.
playback.loop: Declared study interval, forward and reverse, preserving elapsed-time overshoot.
playback.reducedMotion: Paused; user can start playback explicitly.

journey.repeat: Scene fades to black at the orbital seam while the dated pass resets.
journey.interaction: Pause holds camera and clock; Explore freely or manual input leaves the journey at the displayed pose and time. Replay journey restores the retained composition.

introduction.presentation: Smooth visual emphasis; all eligible families remain present, shared memberships draw one light.
introduction.captions: Median WGS84 model height from the displayed worker packet; median mean period from retained mean motion. Attachments excluded.
introduction.issHandoff: Hold the retained initial UTC for four seconds, label ISS before descent, keep identity into the sky.
